newsitem.title: USA: Morey Amsterdam of Dick Van Dyke Show dies.
newsitem.headline: Morey Amsterdam of Dick Van Dyke Show dies.

text.p: Morey Amsterdam, best known for playing the wise-cracking joke writer Maurice "Buddy" Sorrell on TV's "Dick Van Dyke Show", has died of a heart attack, his son said on Monday. He was 87.
Gregory Amsterdam said his father, who had just returned from a two-week cabaret tour on the east coast, was taken to the Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre on Sunday night where he died.

Although best known as one of the writers on the fictional Alan Brady show, along with Dick Van Dyke's Rob Petrie and Rose Marie's Sally Rogers, Amsterdam had already been a successful stand-up comedian and radio comic for many years.
In all, he was in showbusiness -- from Vaudeville to TV and movies -- for 70 years.
He first entered Vaudeville at the age of 14 in 1922 as a comedian and went on to become one of the most prolific comedy writers, providing material for Will Rogers and Fanny Brice.
He was known as the "Human Joke Machine" because he could tell a joke about any subject on request.
By 1947, Amsterdam had three different daily radio shows and comedian Fred Allen once said: "The only thing I can turn on without getting Amsterdam is the faucet."
From 1957-59 he co-starred in the TV show "Keep Talking" and from 1961-66 was on the "Dick Van Dyke Show" which was created by Carl Reiner.
During the 70s he was a regular on "Hollywood Squares" and continued to play clubs in Las Vegas and Atlantic City.
He is survived by his wife Kay, son Gregory and daughter Cathy.
